preamble: 311-313 Special senses and Higher brain functions
1. ข้อสอบมีทั้งหมด 112 ข้อ
2. ข้อสอบเป็นอังกฤษทั้งหมด
3. มีเวลาในการสอบ 2.5 ชั่วโมง

questions.stem: A 43 years old male has a visual deficit cause by complete lesion of optic tract, which of following term that characterized the deficit?

A patient has a complete lesion of the right optic nerve. When light is shone into the right eye, neither pupil constricts. When light is shone into the left eye, both pupils constrict normally. Which structure is most likely damaged?
A 55-year-old patient presents with a visual field deficit. Imaging reveals a complete lesion in the right optic tract. Which of the following best describes the patient's visual field defect?

A patient presents with an inability to initiate horizontal gaze to the right. The right eye cannot abduct, and the left eye cannot adduct during rightward gaze attempts. The physician suspects a lesion in the brainstem affecting the center responsible for coordinating this movement. Which structure is most likely damaged?
A 22-year-old student looks toward a nearby object to focus on it. Which of the following changes occurs during accommodation for near vision?

choices.C: Increased tension of the suspensory ligaments

questions.stem: A man is involved in a motor vehicle accident and sustains vascular injury to the superior portion of the primary visual cortex. Which of the following is most likely to occur?

choices.E: Contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing

questions.stem: A man is involved in a motorcycle accident and sustains an orbital bone fracture with bleeding around the right optic nerve. Examination reveals complete damage to the right optic nerve. Which of the following pupillary responses would most likely be observed?

choices.A: Normal direct and consensual pupillary light reflexes in both eyes
choices.B: Normal consensual pupillary light reflex in the left eye
choices.C: Loss of direct pupillary light reflex in the left eye
choices.D: Loss of direct pupillary light reflex in the right eye
choices.E: Loss of consensual pupillary light reflex in the right eye

questions.stem: A patient presents with a painless, curtain-like shadow over part of the peripheral visual field, accompanied by flashes of light and new-onset floaters. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient with vitamin A deficiency develops night blindness. Which of the following best describes the state of a photoreceptor cell in darkness?

A 68-year-old woman presents with gradually progressive, painless blurring of vision. Examination reveals an opaque lens with no evidence of retinal or optic nerve abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old child presents with leukocoria (a white pupillary reflex). Fundoscopic examination reveals a retinal mass. Genetic analysis identifies a mutation involving a tumor suppressor gene responsible for regulating the G1-to-S phase transition of the cell cycle. Which gene is most likely affected?

A histological section of an opaque lens shows degeneration and aggregation of lens crystallin proteins with disruption of the normal arrangement of lens fibers. Which condition is most likely responsible for this lens opacity?
A 25-year-old patient is diagnosed with an internal hordeolum. Which of the following structures is most likely affected?
A 72-year-old woman presents with bilateral retinal neovascularization. Which of the following is the most likely underlying systemic disease?
A patient presents with chronic ear discharge and hearing loss. Otoscopic examination reveals a white, keratin-like mass within the middle ear. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient develops loss of taste sensation while the ability to detect odors remains intact. Neurological examination localizes the lesion to the rostral medulla. Which of the following structures is most likely affected?

A 7-year-old child develops hearing loss following recurrent episodes of otitis media. Examination suggests impaired transmission of sound through the middle ear. Which type of hearing loss is most likely?

A 6-year-old child presents with recurrent ear pain and a feeling of fullness in the right ear. Otoscopic examination reveals fluid behind the tympanic membrane. Audiometry shows reduced hearing due to impaired transmission of sound through the middle ear. Which type of hearing loss is most likely?
A patient receiving cisplatin chemotherapy develops progressive hearing loss, particularly affecting high-frequency sounds. Which type of hearing loss is most likely?
A sound wave with a high frequency enters the cochlea. Which part of the basilar membrane is most strongly stimulated?

A 56-year-old woman experiences brief episodes of intense vertigo lasting less than one minute whenever she turns her head in bed or looks upward. The episodes are triggered by changes in head position and are associated with positional nystagmus. Neurological examination is otherwise normal. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause?

choices.C: Displacement of otoconia into a semicircular canal

questions.stem: A 10-year-old child has experienced recurrent ear pain and purulent ear discharge for the past 3 years. Otoscopic examination reveals a persistent perforation of the tympanic membrane with mucopurulent discharge. Culture of the ear discharge grows Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient has complete loss of the ability to perceive taste. Which of the following terms best describes this condition?
Which neurotransmitter is primarily involved in signal transmission from taste receptor cells detecting sour taste?

A 25-year-old man is exposed to a strong odor and detects it within a few seconds. Odorant molecules bind to specific receptors located on the cilia of olfactory receptor neurons in the olfactory epithelium. Which of the following signaling proteins is activated as the first intracellular step in olfactory transduction?
A lesion at the pontomedullary junction affects a cranial nerve pathway involved in taste sensation from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue. Which cranial nerve is most likely involved?

A 28-year-old woman can detect odors normally through either nostril individually. However, she has difficulty comparing the intensity and characteristics of an odor detected simultaneously by the two nostrils. A lesion affecting which of the following structures would most likely produce this deficit?
Which of the following structures is most important for conscious discrimination and identification of different odors?
A person eats a very spicy chili pepper and experiences a burning sensation in the mouth. Which of the following mechanisms best explains this sensation?

choices.A: Activation of TRPV1 receptors on trigeminal nerve endings
choices.B: Activation of taste receptors carried by the chorda tympani nerve
choices.C: Activation of sweet taste receptors on taste buds
choices.D: Activation of mechanoreceptors carried by the glossopharyngeal nerve
choices.E: Activation of olfactory receptors in the nasal cavity

questions.stem: Which type of taste is primarily detected by T2R receptors?
Which structure serves as the first relay station in the olfactory pathway?
In the Papez circuit, which pathway carries information from the entorhinal cortex to the hippocampus?
A patient develops severe polyuria (10 L/day), excessive thirst, and nocturia. Which hypothalamic nucleus is most likely damaged?

While walking through a market, a person smells a strong odor of rotten fish and immediately experiences a strong feeling of disgust and aversion. Which of the following amygdaloid nuclei is most closely associated with this olfactory-mediated emotional response?
A 40-year-old woman presents with marked weight loss and loss of appetite. Lesion of which hypothalamic nucleus is most likely responsible?
Which brain structure is primarily involved in the formation of short-term declarative memories?

A patient is encouraged to attend physical therapy regularly. Each time he successfully completes an exercise session, the therapist praises him. As a result, the patient becomes more likely to continue attending physical therapy. Which of the following learning mechanisms best explains this behavior?

A patient develops a stroke and subsequently speaks fluently with normal speech initiation. However, his speech is often meaningless, and he is unable to understand simple verbal commands. Which aspect of language function is most likely impaired?
Which of the following changes in sleep occurs in older adults?
A person is awake and engaged in active mental activity, such as solving a difficult problem. Which EEG wave is most likely observed?

A patient experiences excessive thirst and frequently seeks water throughout the day. He also urinates frequently. Dysfunction of which of the following hypothalamic nuclei is most likely responsible for the increased drive to drink water?
A patient has a nasal obstruction and cannot detect odors through the nose but can still perceive some flavor while eating. Which olfactory function is primarily impaired?
Which structure connects the anterior thalamus nucleus to the cingulate gyrus?
A patient has difficulty maintaining body temperature when exposed to a cold environment and develops hypothermia. A lesion is suspected in which hypothalamic region?

A patient with schizophrenia has a persistent belief that someone is constantly planning to harm him, despite having no evidence to support this belief. Which of the following dopamine changes is most closely associated with this symptom?

choices.A: Increased dopamine activity in the mesocortical pathway
choices.B: Decreased dopamine activity in the mesolimbic pathway
choices.C: Increased dopamine activity in the mesolimbic pathway
choices.D: Decreased dopamine activity in both mesolimbic and mesocortical pathways
choices.E: Decreased dopamine activity in the mesocortical pathway

questions.stem: A patient with bipolar disorder has difficulty regulating emotions and controlling impulsive behavior. Dysfunction of which brain region is most closely associated with impaired emotional regulation in this disorder?
A patient with Parkinson disease develops persistent anxiety and negative thoughts that interfere with daily activities. Which treatment is most appropriate for managing these psychological symptoms?

A patient is asked to smile and is able to produce a symmetrical smile on command. However, when the patient hears a joke and laughs spontaneously, the smile becomes asymmetrical. Which of the following functions is most likely impaired?

A 25-year-old woman with depression reports that she no longer enjoys playing the guitar, which was previously her favorite hobby. Which combination of neurotransmitters is most closely associated with this symptom?

A patient previously developed an intense fear response after repeatedly being exposed to a threatening stimulus. After repeated exposure to the same stimulus without any harmful consequence, the fear response gradually decreases. Which brain structure is most closely involved in fear extinction?
A person suddenly encounters an aggressive dog and becomes frightened. Which of the following physiological responses is most likely to occur?

A 63-year-old woman develops rapidly progressive memory impairment over several weeks. One month later, she develops difficulty walking, poor coordination, and becomes unable to perform daily activities independently. Brain CT shows only minimal degenerative changes. Which pathological finding is most likely responsible for her condition?
Which of the following best describes the underlying mechanism of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)?

choices.C: Degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presents with progressive difficulty initiating movement, muscular rigidity, and a resting tremor. Which protein is most strongly associated with the underlying pathology?

An elderly patient with Alzheimer disease develops nighttime agitation and difficulty sleeping. The physician chooses an orexin receptor antagonist rather than a benzodiazepine. What is the main reason for avoiding benzodiazepines in this patient?

choices.B: Benzodiazepines may worsen cognitive impairment and increase the risk of delirium
choices.C: Orexin receptor antagonist reverse amyloid-β deposition
choices.E: Orexin receptor antagonists increase acetylcholine release in the hippocampus

questions.stem: Which of the following best distinguishes benzodiazepines from Z-drugs?

choices.A: Benzodiazepines have anticonvulsant effects, whereas Z-drugs are primarily used as hypnotics.
choices.B: Benzodiazepines have a faster onset of action than Z-drugs.
choices.C: Benzodiazepines selectively bind to GABA-A α1 receptors, whereas Z-drugs bind to all GABA-A receptors.
choices.D: Benzodiazepines have no anxiolytic effects, whereas Z-drugs are used to treat anxiety.
choices.E: Z-drugs produce stronger muscle relaxation than benzodiazepines.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old patient has been treated with a first-generation antipsychotic for several years. He gradually develops repetitive, involuntary movements of the tongue, lips, and face. Which mechanism most likely contributes to the development of this adverse effect?

choices.B: Upregulation and increased sensitivity of D2 receptors

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man is asked to plan the steps needed to prepare a meal. He can understand the instructions and perform individual actions, but he has difficulty organizing the sequence, keeping information in mind, and adjusting his plan when the situation changes. Which brain region is most likely involved?

A 64-year-old man develops a speech disturbance after a stroke. He understands spoken language and can follow simple commands. However, his speech is slow and effortful. When asked what he wants to drink, he says, “Water… want… water… please.” When asked to repeat the sentence “The sky is blue,” he is unable to repeat it correctly. Which type of aphasia is most likely?

A 68-year-old woman develops a speech disturbance after a stroke. She speaks rapidly and fluently but has poor comprehension. When asked what she had for breakfast, she says, “The table is singing with the window because yesterday is running.” She cannot follow a simple verbal command or repeat the sentence “The boy is eating an apple.” Which type of aphasia is most likely?

A neighbor brings a patient to the hospital because he is unable to unlock the door and enter his house. The patient is awake and fully conscious. When shown a lock and a key, he correctly identifies both objects and explains that a key is used to unlock the door. However, when asked to demonstrate how to unlock the door, he uses inappropriate methods instead of using the key. Which clinical syndrome is most likely present?

A patient is asked to demonstrate how to comb his hair using his right hand. He correctly understands the task but performs an awkward and incorrect hand gesture instead of mimicking the use of a comb. When asked to demonstrate cutting paper with scissors using his left hand, he uses his index and middle fingers as if they were scissors. Muscle strength and sensation are intact. Which clinical syndrome is most likely present?

A patient with epilepsy is started on an antiseizure medication that induces hepatic cytochrome P450 enzymes and can increase its own metabolism after repeated administration. Which of the following drugs is best known for this property?
Which of the following is a characteristic adverse effect of phenytoin?
A patient with chronic liver disease develops significant hypoalbuminemia. He is taking phenytoin for seizure control. Which of the following changes is most likely to occur?

choices.C: Decreased hepatic metabolism of all drugs
choices.E: Increased renal excretion of protein-bound phenytoin

questions.stem: A 28-year-old man is brought to the emergency department with continuous generalized tonic-clonic seizure activity for more than 5 minutes. He remains unresponsive between seizures. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial pharmacological treatment?

A medical student becomes worried about an upcoming examination. Instead of continuously thinking about the examination, she consciously decides to go for a run, then returns home and studies with better concentration. Which defense mechanism is best illustrated?

A patient experiences recurrent palpitations and visits a physician for evaluation. After a complete examination, the physician explains that there is no evidence of a significant medical disorder. However, the patient remains convinced that he has a serious illness and searches the internet for medical terms to explain his symptoms. Which condition is most likely present?

A 35-year-old man is fired from his job because of repeated poor performance. However, he refuses to accept that his own performance contributed to his dismissal and insists that his coworkers deliberately caused him to lose his job because they were jealous of him. Which defense mechanism is most likely being used?
A 20-year-old man has been dependent on alcohol for 2 years and has stopped working and taking responsibility for his daily life. According to Freud’s psychosexual theory, which stage is he in?
A 20-year-old man is easily angered, stubborn, and frequently argues with others. According to Freud's psychosexual theory, which stage is most closely associated with this personality pattern?
A 20-year-old woman enjoys spending time with her boyfriend and developing an intimate romantic relationship. According to Freud’s psychosexual theory, which stage is she in?

A 19-year-old woman who experienced sexual abuse several months ago develops intense fear, tachycardia, and severe anxiety whenever she recalls the traumatic event or encounters reminders of it. Which brain structure is most directly involved in generating this exaggerated fear response?
A patient believes that people on television are talking specifically about him, even though there is no evidence that the program is related to him. Which symptom is most likely present?
A patient with schizophrenia believes that other people can hear or know his thoughts even when he does not speak them aloud. Which symptom is most likely present?
A patient with schizophrenia speaks very little and gives brief responses despite being able to understand the questions. Which negative symptom is most likely present?
A 30-year-old man has a long history of alcohol dependence and drinks alcohol regularly. Which dopaminergic pathway is primarily involved in the reward and addictive effects of alcohol?

choices.C: Ventral tegmental area → Caudate nucleus → Dorsal striatum
choices.D: Ventral tegmental area → Caudate nucleus → Prefrontal cortex
choices.E: Ventral tegmental area → Nucleus accumbens → Prefrontal cortex

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man has had an elevated mood for 1 week. He sleeps only 2–3 hours but feels energetic, talks rapidly, jumps from topic to topic, and believes he has special abilities. His behavior causes significant problems at work and with his family. Which brain region is most closely associated with these symptoms?

A 25-year-old man has had auditory hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized behavior, and negative symptoms for several weeks. His symptoms have caused significant impairment in his social and occupational functioning. Which combination of symptoms fulfills the requirement for the characteristic symptoms of schizophrenia during the active phase?
Which of the following antipsychotic drugs has a distinct pharmacological activity as a dopamine D2 receptor partial agonist?

A 76-year-old woman with early-stage Alzheimer disease has been receiving treatment for several months. She subsequently develops persistent agitation, including verbal outbursts and aggressive behavior that significantly interfere with her daily activities. Non- pharmacological measures have been insufficient. Which of the following medications is most appropriate for managing her agitation?
A traveler develops insomnia after crossing several time zones. Which medication is most appropriate for managing jet lag?
A patient develops severe CNS depression after an overdose of diazepam. Which drug is the most appropriate antidote?
A patient has been taking citalopram for a prolonged period. Which adverse effect is of greatest concern with high-dose or prolonged therapy?
A patient with Alzheimer disease has progressive cognitive impairment and is being considered for memantine therapy. Which is the most appropriate indication?

choices.A: Early-stage Alzheimer disease with mandatory ARIA monitoring
choices.B: Early-stage Alzheimer disease without ARIA monitoring
choices.C: Moderate-to-severe Alzheimer disease with appropriate monitoring
choices.D: Moderate-to-severe Alzheimer disease without any monitoring

questions.stem: A 35-year-old patient with major depressive disorder is prescribed amitriptyline. Which mechanism best explains the antidepressant effect of this medication?

choices.B: Blockade of norepinephrine and serotonin reuptake

questions.stem: A patient develops marked euphoria, increased alertness, and tachycardia shortly after using cocaine. Which mechanism best explains the increased monoamine activity produced by cocaine?

choices.A: Increased synthesis of dopamine and norepinephrine
choices.B: Inhibition of DAT, NET, and SERT

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man develops facial flushing, headache, and palpitations shortly after drinking a small amount of alcohol. This reaction is more common in individuals with an inherited defect in which enzyme?

A 24-year-old man has consumed several cups of coffee every day for years. He decides to stop drinking coffee completely. One day later, he develops marked fatigue, headache, and difficulty concentrating. Which phenomenon best explains these symptoms?
A patient takes amphetamine to increase alertness and concentration. Which mechanism contributes to its stimulant effects?

choices.A: Inhibition of monoamine oxidase, reducing monoamine degradation

questions.stem: A 10-year-old child with ADHD is started on methylphenidate. Which mechanism best explains its therapeutic effect?

choices.A: Inhibition of DAT and NET, increasing dopamine and norepinephrine in the synaptic cleft
choices.B: Activation of DAT and NET, decreasing dopamine and norepinephrine
choices.C: Inhibition of MAO-A, increasing serotonin only
choices.E: Inhibition of VMAT2, preventing monoamine storage

questions.stem: A 72-year-old patient has Alzheimer disease with mild cognitive impairment and confirmed amyloid-β pathology. Which stage of Alzheimer disease is most appropriate for initiating lecanemab therapy?

choices.A: Preclinical Alzheimer disease without cognitive symptoms
choices.B: Mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer disease

questions.stem: A patient with major depressive disorder starts fluoxetine. Although serotonin reuptake is inhibited shortly after treatment begins, significant improvement in mood usually takes several weeks. Which mechanism best explains this delayed therapeutic effect?
A patient is taking amitriptyline for depression and haloperidol for psychotic symptoms. Although these drugs have different primary mechanisms of action, they share which pharmacological effect?
Which adverse drug reaction is most likely to require discontinuation of THC treatment?
Which of the following cannabinoids is most closely associated with an effect on psychotic symptoms?
Which of the following is an endogenous cannabinoid produced naturally in the human body?

A cannabis extract produced by the Government Pharmaceutical Organization (GPO) contains THC 2.7 mg/mL and CBD 2.5 mg/mL. Which of the following conditions is an appropriate indication for cannabinoid therapy?
Which of the following antiemetic drugs is a cannabinoid?
